description: A holon flow checkpoint (one intent slug and its flow worktree) can be driven by two runners at once: both pass the resume checks, both dispatch the same stage, and the second run writes duplicate branches and plan or execution rows that later fail ambiguity checks. A run that halts also leaves its docker run clients and role containers alive, and those containers keep mounting the flow worktree.
goal: Give each flow checkpoint a single runner. (1) A holon flow run takes an exclusive advisory lock per intent slug for its whole life, stored in the repository's git common directory so every worktree sees it, and records the holder's pid, host, start time, slug and worktree in the lock. (2) A second holon flow for the same slug, whether a fresh run, --from-stage or --checkpoint, exits non-zero before any stage runs or any branch, checkpoint or ledger is written, and its message names the holder pid and the lock file. (3) A lock whose holder pid is dead, or whose flock is no longer held, is taken over and the takeover is logged. Different slugs in one repository never block each other. The per-repository admission lock in flow/admission_lock.py is unchanged. (4) When a run halts, fails or receives SIGINT or SIGTERM, it terminates the child processes it started: the process group of each spawned subprocess, the docker run client of each role container, and each role container it launched (stopped by a name or label it set at launch), so no holon flow or docker run child and no container mounting the flow worktree survives the exit. (5) Existing modules listed in holon-config/hygiene/module_budgets.json at their frozen override size (cli/commands/_flow_worktree.py, launcher/containers.py, turns.py) must not grow past that override; put new logic in new modules and keep any edit to those files net-zero or smaller. holon-config/hygiene/module_budgets.json itself is frozen and must not be changed.
rationale: Two runners on one checkpoint have already produced ambiguous plan and execution branches that halted a run and left a pull request with duplicate plan files, and a halted run has left role containers running against a worktree that the next run then found dirty. A per-checkpoint lock that the kernel releases on process death, plus reaping of the run's own children on exit, removes both failure modes without changing the stage pipeline.
acceptance_criteria: Two holon flow runs for the same intent slug in one repository: the second exits non-zero before any stage runs, names the holder pid and the lock file in its message, and writes no branch, checkpoint or ledger row.
Runs for different slugs in the same repository hold their locks concurrently and neither refuses the other.
A lock left by a dead pid is taken over on the next run, and the takeover is logged; a lock held by a live pid is never taken over.
The lock is released on normal exit, on a stage failure, and on SIGINT or SIGTERM; a following run for the same slug proceeds.

After a halted run exits, no child process it started remains: a hermetic test with a fake docker binary and a spawned child process shows both are terminated, and each launched container is stopped by its name or label.
Modules at their frozen override size keep their line counts at or below the override, and new logic lives in the new modules; holon-config/hygiene/module_budgets.json is unchanged.
Hermetic tests cover the lock, takeover, refusal, and reaping paths and run via 'uv run pytest' with no network access; 'uv run task lint' passes.
